payload.claim: `batch_spend` is documented as the source the loop's live budget gate will poll while the batch is still running (its docstring and the acceptance criterion both say so), but the SQL sums `attempts.cost_usd_est`, a column that is NULL until `close_attempt` writes it (schema line 88). Any attempt still open when the gate polls — the normal case under concurrency, since a batch is defined as spanning a concurrency pool — contributes nothing to the sum, so `batch_spend` silently reports less than the money actually committed for the night. Fixture tests only ever call `batch_spend` after `close_attempt`, so this never surfaces there; in production, with several cells running at once, the gate will systematically under-count in-flight spend and could let the loop start more work than the budget allows before the first attempt closes and the omission corrects itself.
